translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses, a speaking.
translations.2: Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the burnt-offering — it shall be placed upon a fire upon the altar throughout the night until the morning, and the fire of the altar shall burn upon it.
translations.3: And the imām shall put on a linen shirt and linen trousers he shall wear upon his body; and he shall remove the ash which the fire of the burnt-offering has consumed upon the altar, and set it beside the altar.
translations.4: Then he shall take off his garments and put on other garments, and carry the ash out to the outside of the camp, to a clean place.
translations.5: And the fire which is upon the altar shall burn therein — it shall not be extinguished; and the imām shall kindle upon it wood every morning, and arrange upon it the burnt-offering, and burn upon it the fat of the peace-offering.
translations.6: And so the fire shall burn upon the altar continually — it shall not be extinguished.
translations.7: And this is the law of the gift-offering: the sons of Aaron shall present it before God, before the altar.
translations.8: And he shall lift from it with his handful, from its fine flour and its oil, and burn its fragrance upon the altar — accepted and pleasing to God.
translations.9: And the remainder of it Aaron and his sons shall eat; it shall be eaten unleavened in a consecrated place — in the court of the tent of the presence they shall eat it.
translations.10: It shall not be baked leavened; I have appointed it as their portion from my offerings — it is among the choicest of the sacred things, like the purification-offering and the guilt-offering.
translations.11: Every male among the sons of Aaron shall eat it — a statute forever for your generations, from the offerings of God; everyone who touches it shall become consecrated.
translations.12: Then God spoke to Moses, a speaking.
translations.13: This is the offering of Aaron and his sons which he shall bring to God on the day of his anointing: a tenth of a waybah of fine flour — a gift continually, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
translations.14: On a pan, with oil it shall be made; in layers you shall bring it — crumbled, it shall be a gift of fragments; you shall present it as accepted and pleasing to God.
translations.15: And likewise the imām who is appointed as his successor from his sons shall make it — a statute forever; it shall be burned entirely to God.
translations.16: And the rest of the imām's gift-offerings shall be burned entirely and shall not be eaten.
translations.17: Then God spoke to Moses, a speaking.
translations.18: Say to Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the purification-offering — in the place where the burnt-offering is slaughtered, the purification-offering shall be slaughtered before God; it is among the choicest of the sacred things.
translations.19: The imām who offers it as a purification-offering shall eat it; it shall be eaten in a consecrated place — in the court of the tent of the presence.
translations.20: Everyone who approaches its flesh shall become consecrated; and if any of its blood that is sprinkled from it should spatter upon a garment, then it shall be washed in a consecrated place.
translations.21: And earthenware vessels in which it is cooked shall be broken; and if it was cooked in a copper vessel, then it shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
translations.22: Every male among the imāms shall eat it, since it is among the choicest of the sacred things.
translations.23: But every purification-offering of which any blood is brought into the tent of the presence, to seek atonement in the sanctuary — it shall not be eaten; rather it shall be burned with fire.
